source: Agriculture Sector Development Project (ASDP), ADB Loan No. 2023-CAM(SF), Guide No.1: Coconut-damaging beetle and protective measures, prepared by Kampot Province Department of Agricultural Extension, 2008
text:
The guide opens with an overview of the many household and farm uses of every part of the coconut tree (ដើមដូង), organized by tree part:

Leaves (ស្លឹកដូង): woven into decorative items and small crafts, used for wrapping/packaging (e.g. wrapping cakes), made into decorative ornaments, and the midrib/leaf spine used to make baskets, racks, and skewers/darts.

Trunk/stem (ទងដូង): used to build fences, woven into baskets, made into planting containers or troughs (ធ្វើទ្រុងជីកបុស្តិ), and burned as firewood/charcoal (អុសដុត).

Roots and soil-holding function (ថែក្សដូង): the root system is credited with helping bind soil and prevent erosion on riverbanks and sloped land, in addition to root use in traditional remedies, basket-making, spoon/ladle carving, decorative carving, and construction material.

Fruit and other products (ផ្សេងៗពីដូង): young coconut water and flesh consumed fresh or made into traditional medicine; the shell processed into canned/bottled coconut water products; mature coconut flesh used to make cakes and desserts; coconut oil extracted and used to make soap; coconut shell fashioned into scoop/ladle vessels (ត្រទាលកដូង) and musical instruments; and coconut husk fiber (ស្រកីដូង) twisted into rope, made into brooms, and used as planting-hole/potting material.

This overview establishes why protecting coconut palms from pest damage matters economically to farming households: nearly every part of the tree has household or income-generating value.
